messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a spike of `invoke_schema_mismatch` rejects in canary for fncall routes. They aren't mapping to any existing fallback policy so requests are failing without graceful degrade. looking for quick sync and whether we should change billing for these.
maya: ugh. do you have an example payload and the validator error? paste it here if possible
kevin: sure — here's the error snippet (sanitized):
```
{"error":"invoke_schema_mismatch","route":"/v1/chat.invoke","expected":"{tool:object}","got":"[object,array]","sample_id":"abc123"}
```
maya: thanks. two quick things: 1) do we treat this as user error (billable) or server-side reject (no charge)? 2) what telemetry are we emitting for these so we can alert on canary noise
ellie: my vote: treat schema rejects the same as other validation rejects — don't bill. they didn't consume model tokens successfully. but we should confirm with billing team.
arjun: +1 on not billing. operationally we should map this error to a soft-fallback first: try permissive coercion adapter for canary routes, increment a metric, and only hard-reject after X retries. also tag rejects with route, model, validator-version, and canary=false/true.
sree: for telemetry names, propose `toolcall.rejects.schema_type` with a tag `schema_error=invoke_schema_mismatch` and `fallback_attempted=true|false`. also emit a counter `toolcall.rejects.sampled_payloads` when we snapshot the request for debugging.
kevin: good. i also want a console UX: when a specific route exceeds 0.1% schema rejects over a 1h window show a yellow banner in Route Insights with link to sample payloads and a rollout toggle. ops can flip to permissive adapter for that route.
maya: banner makes sense. small UX ask: make the toggle scoped to customer+route, not global, otherwise we'll hide failures for other customers.
arjun: about sampling — we should sample 1% of rejects by default but ramp to 10% for canary traffic or if the reject rate > 0.5%. ensure payloads are redacted and stored for 30d with ACL.
ellie: dashboard/alerts — create an SLO-based alert: alert when `toolcall.rejects.schema_type{route=\"/v1/chat.invoke\"}` > 0.1% for 1h AND absolute rejects > 50. send to eng-platform and se-alerts.
kevin: good. also onboarding/rollouts: for canary we should auto-apply permissive adapter only to canary cohort for 24h and record whether permissive conversion succeeded. if conversion success rate < 97% revert and surface to oncall.
sree: small implementation detail — our existing validator returns `field_path` and `suggested_coercion`. include both in sampled payloads to help patch adapters quickly.
maya: question about quotas: if we attempt permissive coercion and it succeeds, do we charge the user for the retried model call? my read: yes — only bill when a model call is actually sent. log a distinct metric `toolcall.coercion.applied` and `billing_event=true|false`.
arjun: agree. if we never reached model runtime (hard reject) then no billing. update RPC semantics: `invoke` response should include `billing_status` for clarity.
ellie: action items: 1) kevin to file infra ticket to map invoke_schema_mismatch -> soft-fallback adapter for canary routes and add metrics/flags. 2) sree to spec telemetry tags and sampling policy. 3) maya to prototype console banner + per-customer toggle. 4) arjun to update billing docs and ensure no-charge on hard rejects.
kevin: i'll make the ticket and link PRs. target: small canary change next week and dashboard alert before EOD Friday.
maya: :thumbsup: will mock up banner copy and toggle flow in product channel.
api-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-25T10:00Z pending PR approvals :eyes:
kevin: thanks everyone. if we see any other schema types spike (coercion_needed, missing_required_field) let's add them to the same metric family so dashboards stay consistent. closing the loop once tickets exist.
ellie: :+1:
arjun: :raised_hands:
